note.headline: Chip stocks drag the tape higher while the curve flattens and the dollar bids
note.standfirst: The S&P 500 added +1.31% and the Nasdaq 100 jumped +2.28% on a semiconductor and megacap rally led by ORCL and AMD, while breadth confirmed the move with 21 advancers against 4 decliners. Underneath, the dollar index rose to a session high and the curve flattened further, a combination that argues for a market pricing good news on growth without yet trusting it on rates.
takeaways: Equities rallied broadly with breadth 5.25 to 1, led by chip and software names rather than defensives.
The 2s10s curve flattened 3bp to 32bp even as long yields held flat, a rates market still wary of duration.
The dollar index hit a session high at 102.91 while EUR/USD and USD/CNY made session lows, the opposite of a typical risk-on dollar reaction.
Vol cratered across the complex, VIX down 10.12% to 17.49, cheapening protection into a market that just repriced higher.
note.desk_view:
This session confirms the equity rally is real and broad, not a single-stock story. Breadth at 5.25 advancers to decliners and gains across nine of eleven sectors say the bid had legs beyond ORCL's +8.82% and AMD's +7.32%. Technology led at +3.23% but cyclicals participated too, industrials up +1.33% and energy up +1.87% alongside a +0.44% rise in WTI. The tell against a clean risk-on read is the dollar. DXY rose +0.67% to a session high while EUR/USD and USD/CNY sat at session lows, and that is not the pattern of a market selling the dollar to buy risk. It is a market buying both.

The level that decides which story wins is 10-year yields. They sit at 4.88%, flat on the day's shift column, with the curve still flattening on the front end, 2-year yields firmer by the prior day's 5bp move. If the dollar bid is a funding story rather than a growth story, long yields stay anchored and risk can keep grinding. If the dollar bid turns out to be the first sign of a tightening in financial conditions, the next leg shows up in credit spreads before it shows up in equities. HYG and LQD both ticked higher today, +0.22% and +0.08%, so credit has not flagged it yet. Watch that series first.
watching: Whether USD strength persists or reverses once Tokyo and London reopen, given USD/JPY's push to 159.70.
Credit spread behavior in HYG and LQD for any divergence from the equity rally.
The next leg in the flattening 2s10s, now at 32bp, for confirmation this is a genuine growth repricing versus a funding squeeze.
Follow-through in semiconductor leadership, ORCL and AMD specifically, versus mean reversion in megacap laggards MSFT and META.
note.equities:
The S&P 500 closed at 7619.38, up +1.31%, with the Nasdaq 100 outperforming at +2.28% on the back of ORCL's +8.82% and AMD's +7.32% moves, both far ahead of the sector average. The Russell 2000 added +0.88% and the S&P MidCap 400 rose +0.84%, so the rally was not confined to megacap tech, though the dispersion inside tech itself was wide: NVDA and AVGO rode the same wave at +2.87% and +3.99% while MSFT and META gave back -2.26% and -1.97%.

Breadth was decisive at 21 advancers to 4 decliners, a 5.25 ratio that confirms participation beyond the leaders. Nine of eleven sectors closed higher, with only consumer discretionary at -0.05% and real estate essentially flat at +0.02% lagging. Health care barely moved at +0.04% despite sitting at a session high in the broader extremes list, a sign the sector's strength is relative rather than absolute today.
note.rates:
The curve flattened again, 2s10s down 3bp to 32bp and 5s30s down 3bp to 59bp, continuing a trend rather than starting one. The belly underperformed modestly, with 2-year and 5-year yields firmer by 5bp and 3bp respectively on the prior session's shift, while 10-year and 30-year yields were closer to flat.

Breakevens softened across the board: the 10-year breakeven fell 2bp to 2.20% and the 5y5y forward fell 4bp to 2.15%, while 10-year TIPS real yields rose 3bp to 2.66%. That combination, real yields up and breakevens down, is a hawkish mix for a session where equities rallied hard, and it sits awkwardly next to the MOVE index rise of +7.50% even as realized vol in stocks collapsed.
note.credit: Spreads firmed modestly and the tone was constructive without being euphoric. HYG rose +0.22% and JNK +0.22%, LQD added +0.08%, and EMB, the EM sovereign proxy, ticked up +0.10%. Leveraged loans gained +0.10%. None of this is a stretch move, and credit's muted response next to a +2.28% Nasdaq print is worth noting as the more sober read of the day.
note.fx: The dollar index rose +0.67% to 102.91, a session high, and the move was broad: EUR/USD fell -1.16% to a session low at 1.109, GBP/USD dropped -1.23%, and AUD/USD slipped -1.03%. USD/JPY climbed +1.09% to 159.70, USD/CHF rose +1.57% to a session high, and USD/CAD added +0.88%, also a session high. In EM, USD/BRL rose +1.35%, USD/TRY sat at a session high, while USD/CNY made a session low at 6.67, the one major pair where the dollar lost ground.
note.commodities: Energy firmed with WTI up +0.44% to 86.42 and Brent up +1.25% to 92.63, while natural gas fell -1.55%. Gold slipped -0.89% to 3994.30 even as silver rose +1.13% to 51.68, an unusual split inside precious metals. Copper added +0.75% to 6.266, consistent with the broader cyclical bid in equities. Ags were mixed: wheat rose +1.35%, cocoa jumped +6.73%, while coffee fell -2.19%.
note.volatility: The vol complex came in hard. VIX fell -10.12% to 17.49 and VIX9D dropped -13.48% to 16.04, with the front end falling faster than the 3-month print at 19.24, down -6.78%. VVIX fell -6.38% and SKEW eased -1.34% to 149.09. The curve's shape, front-month vol below 3-month, says the market is pricing calm near term while still carrying some tail premium further out. Protection got materially cheaper into a rally, which is the normal pattern, not a warning sign on its own.
note.digital: Bitcoin rose +0.50% to 74086.89 and Ether added +0.58%, modest moves that lagged the equity rally by a wide margin. Solana gained +0.80% and XRP was roughly flat at +0.03%. Digital assets traded like a low-beta sidecar to risk today rather than a leveraged expression of it.
note.international: European bourses closed higher across the board ahead of the US session, with the DAX up +1.20% to a session high and the EURO STOXX 50 adding +1.04%. The AEX also hit a session high, up +1.12%. Asia was more mixed: the Nikkei rose +1.31% and the KOSPI jumped +2.60%, TAIEX surged +3.62%, but the Hang Seng fell -0.98%, the one regional laggard. The handoff to New York was a clean risk bid outside China, and the US session built on it rather than reversing it.
note.correlation:
The cross-asset picture split today rather than moved together. Equities, credit, and cyclical commodities all confirmed the same risk-on signal, but the dollar and precious metals did not play along, DXY at a session high while gold fell -0.89%. That is not the textbook risk-on fingerprint, where a weaker dollar typically accompanies an equity rally of this size.

A break in this correlation matters because it changes what hedges actually hedge. If the dollar keeps rising alongside equities, long-dollar positions stop offsetting equity risk the way desks are used to, and EM and commodity-linked trades absorb the strain instead, visible already in USD/BRL and USD/TRY sitting at session highs. Watch whether gold's weakness here is a one-day real-yield story or the start of a divergence that outlasts the equity rally.
